subject: biotechnology
title: Fermentation: Yeast Converts Glucose to Ethanol and Carbon Dioxide Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says The alcohol appears from nothing as the mixture ferments, because the glucose in the flask stays the same while ethanol and gas are produced. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - new products mean material was created from nothing

The yeast converts the glucose: as fermentation proceeds the glucose is used up, and that same material reappears as ethanol in the liquid and carbon dioxide gas collecting above it - glucose falls by the amount converted.
The yeast made the ethanol out of the water in the solution, and the glucose was never used
The gas came from the air above the liquid, not from the flask contents

questions.misconception: The alcohol appears from nothing as the mixture ferments, because the glucose in the flask stays the same while ethanol and gas are produced.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: The alcohol appears from nothing as the mixture ferments, because the glucose in the flask stays the same while ethanol and gas are produced. Reteach point: The yeast converts the glucose: as fermentation proceeds the glucose is used up, and that same material reappears as ethanol in the liquid and carbon dioxide gas collecting above it - glucose falls by the amount converted.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain where the carbon dioxide in the gas space came from.
questions.answer: The yeast produced it by converting glucose: the bubbles formed in the liquid, rose through it and collected in the gas space above the liquid.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the source and the journey: made from converted glucose, risen as bubbles, collected in the gas space.

questions.prompt: At the end of fermentation, the glucose bar is:

choices.text: Still full, exactly as at the start
Almost empty, because the glucose was converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide
Hidden behind the ethanol bar but unchanged

questions.feedback: Scene 4 is careful with the bars: the glucose is almost gone because it was converted - the ethanol bar is high and the gas space is full.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state the final stage of fermentation and what the glucose became.
questions.answer: Fermentation is complete: the glucose has been converted by the yeast into ethanol in the liquid and carbon dioxide collected in the gas space.
questions.feedback: A strong answer gives the whole conversion - glucose used up, ethanol produced, carbon dioxide collected - and names the yeast as the converter.
